a.xlink:title: make_build: reads IDENTITY, DIST_DIR and, when the caller set it, PW_FRESH_BUILD from the make command line or environment; writes nothing; runs build.sh with them
a.text: [build] build, sign and embed evidence into …/PolicyWitness.app

a.xlink:title: admission: reads BUILD_XPC, PW_INSPECTION, PW_FRESH_BUILD and the argument list (--help prints the usage and exits before any check, after the knobs are validated); whether each tracked input the build copies exists; without a claim in the environment, the caller's SDKROOT, CPATH, LIBRARY_PATH, MANPATH and LC_CTYPE, recorded by the shell front end's builtins before any Python runs, and tests/.checkout.lock, which the owner it starts takes before supervising the script again under it; writes the owner record in tests/.checkout.lock (pid, start time and acquisition nonce) for as long as the owner and its protected children hold it; nothing else

lock: reads the owner's handoff over the channel the claim names: the held descriptor, open on this checkout's lock file, the acquisition nonce its owner record carries and the requests the owner bound to that acquisition; never the environment alone; writes SDKROOT, CPATH, LIBRARY_PATH, MANPATH and LC_CTYPE restored to the caller's recorded state; nothing on disk
check_limits: reads docs/limits.json and the documents it renders; writes nothing
check_contract: reads docs/contract.json, docs/architecture.json and their generated copies; writes nothing
check_build_doc: reads docs/build.json, build.sh, meson.build, the Makefile, the inventories, the baseline and the generated copies; writes nothing
check_identity: reads the identity inputs and the three generated copies; writes nothing

stamp: reads git describe, rev-parse and rev-list, or PW_VERSION and PW_BUILD_NUMBER from the environment; writes the four stamp variables for Cargo and the plists; after admitting builddir/, controller/target/, its release/ and the session destination, controller/target/ when it is missing and the build session file, opened with the stamp, the three knobs, the acquisition nonce and the owner's requests
minimum: reads LSMinimumSystemVersion in Info.plist; writes MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET for Cargo

sdk: reads the SDK path and numeric version xcrun reports under DEVELOPER_DIR for the macosx default, or for the SDK a caller's SDKROOT names; writes SDKROOT for Cargo and Meson, resolved by xcrun, and the SDK version every shipped output must carry

builddir: reads in incremental mode: builddir/meson-info/meson-info.json and builddir/pw-toolchain.json when the directory is configured, and the stamped SDK, developer directory, compiler commands and Rust compiler probed now; in fresh mode nothing, since the directory is replaced; writes the toolchain observation into the build session
identity: reads IDENTITY and the keychain listing; the knobs, for Meson's options and RUSTFLAGS; writes RUSTFLAGS, when inspection is on and it was unset or empty, and the record of who set it

cargo_admit: reads Cargo's configuration as one invocation from this directory reads it: `.cargo/config` or `config.toml` here, in each ancestor and in Cargo home, with their includes, merged by Cargo's precedence; the environment overrides; the launcher (a rustup proxy and the toolchain it resolves); and cargo metadata's report of the target and build directories under the pinned target directory; writes the compiler and wrapper selection with its sources, the `[env]` entries and whether each applied, the compiler's inputs in Cargo's child environment, the requested Rust flags by precedence and the admission, into the build session
a.text: Admitting the Cargo output and intermediate directories: …

a.xlink:title: fresh: reads builddir/ and controller/target/release/, admitted again with every component below the checkout a real directory of this user, or absent, both before either is removed, and rechecked before each removal; writes removes both directories through their admitted descriptors; records each one's replacement in the build session; nothing else is removed

cargo: reads cargo on PATH with its configuration, caches and registries; controller/ sources, the stamp variables, MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET, SDKROOT and RUSTFLAGS; the artifact paths and per-target reuse judgments Cargo reports, each a literal boolean bound to the shipped target, a profile and the admitted executable, and Cargo's fingerprint for each shipped target; writes controller/target/release/ under the pinned output directory, the messages file Cargo reports its artifacts in, and the judgments into the build session
toolchain: reads meson and ninja on PATH and ninja's version; writes nothing
a.text: Checking the native toolchain (meson, ninja … or newer)

a.xlink:title: configure: reads whether builddir/build.ninja exists, meson.build, meson.options and the two Meson options; a fresh setup also reads CFLAGS and the other flag variables, and the compilers Meson selected; writes builddir/ configuration; a fresh setup publishes builddir/pw-toolchain.json atomically from the selected compilers, SDK and Rust compiler; meson configure records the two options and the policy assertions run at setup or at the regeneration the next compile triggers
a.text: Configuring native build (meson configure, existing directory): …

a.xlink:title: compile: reads the native sources through builddir/; a changed option triggers regeneration, which runs the policy assertions first; writes builddir/ outputs and the Swift module cache under it

native_check: reads Meson's introspection of builddir/, Ninja's dependency log, the identity inputs, the stamp and the compilers the directory records, and every shipped output's load commands; writes builddir/pw-toolchain.json extended with the Swift compiler a reused directory discovered when this build enabled the XPC pieces, atomically and without changing another field; the toolchain, option and SDK observations into the build session
a.text: Checking the configured native source lists and the identity closure against the tree

a.xlink:title: assemble: reads Info.plist, the three Rust outputs, runner/augments/, dist/README.md and dist/AGENTS.md, all admitted before the first check; writes the two documents under DIST_DIR; removes the previous app, ZIP and guide; the stamped Info.plist, the three Rust executables and the augments under the new app
embed_client: reads builddir/pw-runner-client; writes Contents/MacOS/pw-runner-client and its dSYM in inspection builds
skip_xpc: reads nothing; writes nothing

embed_services: reads each service's Info.plist and builddir/ host, the worker, validator and issuer; writes each service bundle: its stamped Info.plist, the host with its dSYM in inspection builds, the worker, validator and issuer
presign: reads the identity inputs and copies, the generated identity in tests/lib/contract.py and the built worker's --version report; writes nothing
a.text: Checking host/worker identity again, before signing

a.xlink:title: sign_tools: reads the copied top-level helpers; writes signatures on the top-level helpers
sign_services: reads each service's Entitlements.plist, admitted before the first check, and the assembled bundle; writes signatures on the nested helpers, then each service seal

evidence: reads the signed bytes, entitlements and exported symbols of the helpers, services and augments; the build session; every shipped output's load commands and signature display; the caller's requests and Cargo's effective deployment target and SDK, from the build session; writes Contents/Resources/Evidence/manifest.json, symbols.json and provenance.json, the manifest listing the other two; the record only after it passes its own validation
a.text: Writing evidence manifest and provenance record

a.xlink:title: seal: reads PolicyWitness.entitlements; writes the app seal over everything under Contents/
verify: reads the sealed app; writes nothing
signer: reads every regular file under the app's and each service's Contents/MacOS, and the app and service seals, as codesign displays them; writes nothing
sign_observer: reads controller/target/release/sandbox-log-observer; writes that executable's signature, in place
guide: reads docs/PolicyWitness.md and its inputs; writes PolicyWitness.md under DIST_DIR
zip: reads the sealed app; writes PolicyWitness.zip under DIST_DIR
